subject: Types
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.5.3.1 'Currency symbols match if and only if the corresponding currency strings are the same' -> OK §8.5.3.1 1)). Code: PictureAnalyzer canonicalizes every currency SYMBOL in the mask to '$' and records the currency STRING in PicInfo.CurrencyString (null when the string is '$'); StrongTypeModel.SameAnalyzedProfile compares the PicInfo record (canonical EditMask + CurrencyString), so the match is by string, not by symbol - exactly the rule. The only cross-configuration site is two SEPARATE outermost source elements (§12.3.7.4 GR1 makes a contained unit inherit the container's currency signs), reached through a program-prototype CALL whose strongly-typed formal runs OoConformance.StrongTypeMismatch -> StrongTypeModel.SameType. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, E:\Temp\claude\E--COBOL\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2\out\probe\types): TPD caller default currency 'PIC $$9' vs callee CURRENCY SIGN IS "$" WITH PICTURE SYMBOL "U" 'PIC UU9' (different symbols, same string) -> compiles and runs 'OK' (expected: match, conforms); TPE caller '$'->"$" vs callee CURRENCY SIGN IS "#" WITH PICTURE SYMBOL "$" both 'PIC $$9' (same symbol, different strings) -> COBOL1688 strongly-typed argument not of the same type (expected: no match, conforms). Both directions verified. No existing spec-derived test exercises the currency exception (grep of tests/ for TYPEDEF together with CURRENCY SIGN finds none) -> test-ref empty.
